levels.name: deterministic
levels.scope: Risk arithmetic, current-policy admission, ledger atomicity and agent permissions. No broker connection.

levels.name: protocol
levels.scope: Real service process and IBKR HTTP adapter against a documented local simulator. No real broker connection.

levels.name: paper_preflight
levels.scope: Authenticated IBKR paper identity, contract lookup and non-submitting what-if requests.

levels.name: paper_lifecycle
levels.scope: Supervised MCP paper lifecycle with independent order, execution, fee, position and cash reconciliation. A submit/cancel smoke alone is incomplete.

levels.name: operational
levels.scope: Multi-session recovery, stale/external broker state, whole-account limits, alerting, halt and restore acceptance.

levels.name: live_canary
levels.scope: Separate owner-authorized bounded real-money canary after all prior gates; never automatically run by CI.

cases.scenario: Risk cap tightened after funding
cases.acceptance: Submission revalidates current policy; zero risk blocks the mock broker call, accounting for the trade's own reservation exactly once.

cases.scenario: Missing mandatory policy
cases.acceptance: Production trading configuration refuses new exposure when required caps are absent or unreadable.

cases.scenario: Per-order boundary and smallest supported increment above it
cases.acceptance: At-cap request is admitted only when all other constraints pass; over-cap request leaves ledger unchanged and makes zero broker calls.

cases.scenario: Many individually permissible orders exceed aggregate risk
cases.acceptance: Reservations, pending orders and positions are aggregated per broker account across all agents and Trust accounts.

cases.scenario: Policy changed while request waits in queue
cases.acceptance: Worker checks current policy at dispatch; an earlier preview is never sufficient authorization.

cases.scenario: Reservation or risk approval expires
cases.acceptance: New submission requires a fresh bounded authorization and cannot reuse an expired approval.

cases.scenario: No fresh broker account or market snapshot
cases.acceptance: New exposure is blocked; verified permitted cancellation and risk-reducing actions remain available.

cases.scenario: Manual or external broker position appears
cases.acceptance: Unknown position is visible in whole-account exposure; new risk stays blocked until reconciled.

cases.scenario: Mixed currency or unknown FX/multiplier
cases.acceptance: No implicit aggregation or assumed multiplier; unsupported conversion is rejected.

cases.scenario: Gap through stop or slippage beyond plan
cases.acceptance: Actual execution loss is booked; risk budget is reduced, with no claim that the stop caps realized loss.

cases.scenario: Risk-increasing amendment or wrong order type
cases.acceptance: Stop widening, increased effective exposure, and unsupported stop/stop-limit semantics are rejected before broker mutation.

cases.scenario: Restart while an operation is unresolved
cases.acceptance: Original identity and uncertainty survive restart; additional exposure for the affected account stays blocked until authoritative resolution.

cases.scenario: Trading agent attempts policy/admin actions
cases.acceptance: OAuth grant and scope checks deny rule changes, ledger deposits, restores and administrator operations.

cases.scenario: Trading agent fabricates a manual fill
cases.acceptance: Manual accounting authority is unavailable to the trading agent; broker reconciliation authority cannot imply arbitrary manual-fill permission.

cases.scenario: Agent attempts direct broker access
cases.acceptance: Network and secret isolation prevent bypassing Trust to reach authenticated broker mutation endpoints.

cases.scenario: Same request repeated concurrently
cases.acceptance: One durable operation and one authorized external attempt; callers observe the original outcome.

cases.scenario: Equivalent requests with different keys or different agents
cases.acceptance: Independent risk reservations still enforce the aggregate cap; the idempotency key is not the risk boundary.

cases.scenario: Prompt injection or explicit ignore-limits instructions
cases.acceptance: Only typed requests reach deterministic validation; text cannot override policy or grant authority.

cases.scenario: Token revoked, expired, wrong audience/account or scope
cases.acceptance: Rejected before financial or broker effects, including expired queued requests.

cases.scenario: False success or timeout supplied by agent
cases.acceptance: State transitions derive from broker evidence and persisted state, never the agent's interpretation.

cases.scenario: Force-refresh returns an empty array
cases.acceptance: Refresh acknowledgment is not treated as a complete empty order snapshot; obtain authoritative evidence or fail closed.

cases.scenario: Complete or partial existing bracket
cases.acceptance: Recover matching complete bracket; partial/ambiguous bracket blocks another submission and triggers reconciliation.

cases.scenario: Duplicate, delayed and reordered fills
cases.acceptance: Execution identity deduplicates bookings; cumulative quantities never regress or overfill silently.

cases.scenario: Fill arrives during position snapshot
cases.acceptance: Stale snapshot cannot erase the new execution, position or owner.

cases.scenario: Partial entry then cancel/fill race
cases.acceptance: Actual terminal quantity and remaining protection reconcile; cancel acknowledgment alone does not release capital.

cases.scenario: Partial exit with sibling stop/target remaining
cases.acceptance: Remaining exposure is represented and protected; no oversized sibling can silently reverse the position.

cases.scenario: Late fees, correction or unsupported activity
cases.acceptance: Documented corrections are idempotent; ambiguous activity blocks unverified accounting assumptions.

cases.scenario: HTTP warning reply instead of order acknowledgment
cases.acceptance: Unapproved warnings are never blindly confirmed; ambiguous submission stays unresolved without a second POST.

cases.scenario: Timeout before dispatch versus after broker acceptance
cases.acceptance: Before dispatch proves no external mutation; after dispatch preserves unknown outcome and original identity.

cases.scenario: Crash before intent, after intent, after broker acceptance, after ledger commit
cases.acceptance: Each cut point preserves durable evidence and avoids silent duplicate execution or duplicate cash booking.

cases.scenario: Audit/disk failure or corrupt persisted record
cases.acceptance: New financial mutation fails closed; restore path preserves evidence and cannot falsely claim a confirmed outcome.

cases.scenario: 429, session expiry, competing login or gateway restart
cases.acceptance: Shared broker pacing and authentication recovery do not retry mutations blindly; new exposure resumes only after identity and state checks.

cases.scenario: Cancellation while entry fills
cases.acceptance: Confirmed executions remain authoritative, and protective orders are retained or reconciled.

cases.scenario: Order/history retention or pagination boundary
cases.acceptance: Incomplete history and partial page reads do not masquerade as a flat account.

cases.scenario: Authenticated paper identity and allowed account
cases.acceptance: Broker-reported isPaper plus exact account allowlist and selected account all agree before any order.

cases.scenario: Contract identity and permissions
cases.acceptance: Confirm conid, currency, multiplier, tick/lot rules, trading permissions and allowed instrument class from broker evidence.

cases.scenario: What-if bracket preview
cases.acceptance: Preview commissions, margin and warnings for exact intended payload; record that preview does not establish order acceptance.

cases.scenario: Authenticated MCP end-to-end submit and cancel
cases.acceptance: Real deployed service, policy, durable journal, IBKR adapter, acknowledgment and terminal cancellation are correlated by operation/order IDs.

cases.scenario: Entry fill and child activation
cases.acceptance: Broker evidence confirms child links, actual filled quantity and protective stop/target activation; paper order acknowledgment alone does not pass.

cases.scenario: Target fill and sibling cancellation
cases.acceptance: Position closes as expected, sibling is confirmed terminal, and executions/fees/ledger reconcile.

cases.scenario: Stop fill and sibling cancellation
cases.acceptance: Record actual execution price and fees, confirm no residual unintended exposure, and update risk budgets.

cases.scenario: Order update and partial-fill scenarios
cases.acceptance: Record the observed broker transitions; a run without the intended partial fill is inconclusive, never marked passed.

cases.scenario: Service and gateway restart with working orders
cases.acceptance: Recover original IDs, maintain existing protection and reconcile before admitting new risk.

cases.scenario: End-of-run independent reconciliation
cases.acceptance: Compare Trust orders, executions, fees, positions and cash against broker account reports with documented precision/timing allowances; unexplained differences fail.

cases.scenario: Owned-order cleanup
cases.acceptance: Cleanup touches only allowlisted test-owned orders; unresolved orders/positions are reported rather than blindly liquidating the account.

cases.scenario: Repeated daily session rollover and authentication expiry
cases.acceptance: Complete operational recovery and reconciliation without unexplained exposure, duplicated execution or silent alert failure.

cases.scenario: Monitor freshness, unresolved outcomes and missing protection
cases.acceptance: Alerts are independently observable and inhibit new exposure within a declared operational budget.

cases.scenario: Emergency halt and permitted risk reduction
cases.acceptance: Halt persists across restart; it stops new entries without automatically canceling protective stops; exits have separate verified authorization.

cases.scenario: Backup restoration into an isolated service
cases.acceptance: Audit continuity and broker identity reconcile before enabling mutations; stale backup does not recreate orders.

cases.scenario: Reference-model and mutation-testing gate
cases.acceptance: Generated event sequences preserve cash/position invariants; removing risk checks or changing comparisons/signs/side mappings is caught by tests.

cases.scenario: Reproducible release evidence
cases.acceptance: Pin source revision plus dirty diff, lockfile hash, policy version, test seed, service version and supported broker scenarios; retain sanitized artifacts.

cases.scenario: Separately authorized live canary
cases.acceptance: Only after preceding gates pass, explicit owner approval defines absolute notional, instrument and time limits with independent monitoring; paper evidence alone is insufficient.

live_blockers: Current balances are local ledger projections; the Broker trait has no complete broker-account cash/positions snapshot contract.
Monthly risk uses UTC ledger entry basis, not broker mark-to-market account drawdown; service admission requires explicit policies, but this is not a broker-equity loss limit.
Background reconciliation iterates known active trades; errors can be logged without a portfolio-wide new-risk halt.
semantics: A passed level establishes only its stated scope. No level guarantees profit, fills or a maximum realized loss. Source changes invalidate prior evidence. Levels 4-6 remain incomplete until all required broker/operational observations are available.
